ranked.headline: Logical teleportation, mediator-assisted logical T gates and multi-qubit gates across platforms
ranked.summary: Lattice-surgery teleportation on 41 superconducting qubits appears alongside proposals for color-code T gates, transversal ion CZ gates and finite-blockade CCZ.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is implementing logical and multi-qubit entangling operations across hardware platforms. The one experimental demonstration teleports logical qubits by lattice surgery between distance-three surface-code patches on 41 superconducting qubits. The remaining gate work consists of proposals addressing other fault-tolerance bottlenecks. A persistent-mediator architecture reuses a 3D color-code block to apply repeated logical T gates to a 2D register, supported by simulations. In a double-well trapped-ion architecture, parallel transversal CZ gates act across neighboring wells, combined with dynamical decoupling and crosstalk mitigation. A reset-assisted scheme uses noisy mediator qubits to drive high-fidelity gates on long-lived data qubits, analyzed with quantum trajectories. For neutral atoms, an analytically specified CCZ gate under finite Rydberg interactions is compared with a fast antiblockade scheme. Separately, an analog Rydberg simulator performs phase estimation of ground-state energies and gaps for up to 19 atoms via Loschmidt echoes. Peripheral items cover Krotov control of GHZ-type XXZ states, bosonic Fock-state stabilization, an Fe2+:forsterite qubit and Majorana-based reservoir computing.

ranked.headline: Exact classical samplers target noisy and near-Clifford error-correction circuits
ranked.summary: Three new simulators handle non-Clifford, coherent and general Kraus noise in QEC-style circuits while remaining exact or reaching distance-9 surface codes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is classical machinery for sampling noisy quantum circuits, with error-correction workloads as the main target. MASQ is an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits that materializes only the non-Clifford contributions relevant to measurements. Compiled Clifford-augmented matrix product states accelerate coherent-noise QEC simulation and reach distance-9 surface codes. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched GPU execution is extended to mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels while remaining exact. A second strand treats quantum hardware or circuits as samplers. One study quantifies how physical qubit embeddings affect annealer sampling of the 2D Ising model and feeds QPU-learned proposals into corrected Monte Carlo. Another trains a hypernetwork that maps Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles for ground-state samplers. A third finds the Fisher trace uninformative for certifying Born machines and shows that kernel verdicts depend on tolerance. Peripheral items cover stopping thresholds for noisy Grover search under Drude-Lorentz noise, commutator-guided repair of shallow circuits, and Koopman-von Neumann flow simulation with surface-code resource estimates.

ranked.headline: Fast, accurate decoders and optimized syndrome circuits push qLDPC codes toward practice
ranked.summary: New decoders such as SCOPE, TEMPO-BP and TCBP-JOBS target qLDPC accuracy under real-time latency, alongside circuit-scheduling and code-design advances.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is decoding quantum LDPC codes accurately within real-time budgets. SCOPE, a physics-informed parallel decoder, reports a logical error rate of 4.82e-10 on the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code with 173.8 ns latency. TEMPO-BP adapts per-variable memory strength through local feedback, outperforming BP+OSD and Relay-BP. TCBP-JOBS learns calibrated fault probabilities on GPUs and matches Tesseract accuracy. A hybrid sliding-window decoder for trapped-ion noise uses soft-output confidence to switch windows, improving on BP-LSD. For surface codes, Beyond Blossom reports a 4.23x geometric-mean speedup for CPU MWPM via local predecoding. A second strand targets syndrome-extraction circuits: Proxima schedules them using a DEM-based proximity metric, and structure-guided CP-SAT synthesis lowers logical error rates for CSS qLDPC codes. Code-design work adds Armillary codes with rates above 1/2 for fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware and rate-optimal distance-3 and distance-4 color codes simulated at break-even.

ranked.headline: Simulations calibrate nuisance biases and secondary halo dependence in LSS probes
ranked.summary: New TNG, HR4, HESTIA and DESI-BGS mock studies quantify n(z), lens-multipole and assembly-bias effects that matter for Euclid- and DESI-era cosmology.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of simulations to quantify systematics and secondary dependencies linking observables to cosmological parameters. For nuisance modelling, on-the-fly Gaussian Process reconstruction of n(z) in Euclid-like 3×2pt analyses shows that redshift-distribution systematics bias w0wa. IllustrisTNG ellipticals indicate that multipole mass terms bias time-delay H0 by 1–6%. For secondary bias, TNG300 shows that the unbound matter fraction in the circum-halo medium largely explains halo secondary bias through cold tidal and hot inertial accretion regimes. Luminosity-weighted marked correlations are proposed as a null test for galaxy assembly bias and are tested on DESI-BGS mocks at 0.1<z<0.4. Direct observation–simulation comparisons find that SDSS genus topology matches modern HR4 galaxy models far better than earlier models, and that HESTIA underpredicts the observed Milky Way excess of close satellite pairs. Peripheral items include a GR test from DESI Legacy Imaging cluster clustering, Gini-index BCG dominance showing no evolution, and Euclid Q1 radio-loud AGN fractions.

ranked.headline: Classical hardware co-designed to decode and track QEC within microsecond budgets
ranked.summary: FPGA neural decoding, multi-GPU belief propagation and Pauli-frame microarchitectures now target sub-microsecond loops for fault-tolerant control.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is co-design of the classical hardware that must keep pace with fault-tolerant quantum processors. On decoding, Rapids pairs a streaming neural decoder with FPGAs to decode surface-code syndromes in under a microsecond, with lower logical error rates than existing decoders. Pêlagos orchestrates relay belief-propagation decoding across multiple GPUs under real-time constraints. A survey organizes hierarchical decoding by decoder- and code-level hierarchy, platform and latency trade-offs. CHEQ evaluates decoders concurrently on an FPGA using geometric-skip circuit-level noise sampling, matching Stim firing rates within 0.16%. QuFrame's control microarchitecture closes the QEC loop within 1 μs via real-time Pauli frame tracking. A second strand covers platform-specific compilation and control: NEAT for AOD transport in neutral-atom arrays, an FPGA-based quantum data processing unit that cuts assembly latency and measures NVQLink round-trip, Lean-verified QCCD co-design (QCCDCert) scaling to 512 qubits, and MLIR-based circuit cutting (QWeaver). Latency and hardware constraints are treated as primary design targets throughout.

ranked.headline: DESI-era data are used to test dark energy evolution against LCDM with models, reconstructions and new SN Ia samples
ranked.summary: Eight November 2026 preprints test evolving dark energy against LCDM with DESI-era data, spanning model comparison, reconstruction and independent SN Ia calibration.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is whether DESI BAO or full-shape data, combined with CMB, supernova and lensing probes, favor dark energy that departs from a cosmological constant. Model-level work compares one-parameter vacuum histories within VCDM, where F42 is favored by AIC with supernovae, and reports that the scalar-field Fading Dark Sector model outperforms CPL w0-wa in a DESI DR1 full-shape analysis. Two non-parametric reconstructions of dark-energy density and gravitational response find a phantom-divide crossing near z≈0.5–0.7, one also asking whether dark energy clusters. A generalised axion-like quintessence model is confronted with multiple datasets. New elements are the independent SN Ia efforts (LEMAITRE; ZTF, SNLS and HSC calibration) targeting the w-w_a tension, and observable-only 0i Einstein-equation tests of dark-sector degeneracies.

ranked.headline: Symmetry and structure cut resource costs in quantum and classical many-body simulation
ranked.summary: Eight preprints use spin symmetry, sparsity and embedding to cut sampling and circuit costs, with hardware demonstrations and classical scaling to over 10^11 Pauli strings.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is exploiting symmetry or problem structure to reduce the cost of many-body simulation. Spin-adapted SqDRIFT completes sampled configurations to enforce S^2 symmetry and return exact spin eigenstates. A separate circuit loads U(1)×SU(2)-symmetric MPS from spin-adapted reduced tensors for fault-tolerant algorithms. Sparse quantum prolate diagonalization uses compressed sensing to reduce sample complexity from O(N_s) to O(log N_s) and is demonstrated on trapped ions. A time-dependent Gutzwiller embedding for Hubbard quenches and RG-guided variational circuits on a 16-qubit IQM device likewise encode physical structure. Quantum-walk search on complete bipartite graphs is realized on a gate-based processor. Classical work provides F2-linear partitioning for Pauli propagation beyond 10^11 strings and an effective Hamiltonian method for 96-transmon quench dynamics.

ranked.headline: Structured hardware noise is being characterized and fed back into QEC, calibration and mitigation
ranked.summary: Eight November 2026 preprints tie measured noise structure, including correlated leakage, to calibration, code geometry, simulation and validation on superconducting devices.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is treating non-ideal hardware noise in error correction and mitigation as structured, measurable and exploitable. A 105-qubit superconducting experiment scales surface-code stability tests to 7x7 patches and identifies temporally correlated heating-to-|3> leakage. Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escapes is implemented on IBM hardware. GEARS uses gate-error amplification with syndrome feedback to recalibrate during QEC, cutting measurement needs about eightfold. Logical error prediction under biased circuit-level noise guides rectangular surface-code geometry selection and reduces qubit overhead. Ellis simulates qubit loss and leakage with a Pauli-frame method. Complementary near-term work extends bnZNE mitigation to randomized circuits and proposes a self-baseline testing oracle with a controlled false-positive rate. The common novelty is linking characterized noise to calibration, resource choices and validation.

ranked.headline: Compilers and certified tools tie resource optimization to correctness in fault-tolerant quantum computing
ranked.summary: Eight preprints pair circuit and code optimization with formal or exact verification, spanning Lean-checked compilation, Shor harnesses and stabilizer distance certification.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is fault-tolerant quantum software in which resource reduction is coupled to correctness guarantees. Compilation work includes MARBLE, which synthesizes OpenQASM block encodings from matrix formulas, qlin, which rewrites dynamic-circuit branches and decoders with a Lean 4-verified translation validator, and PRISM, which keeps multiple logical-gate realizations open during dual-rail routing. Verification efforts include a formally verified Shor order-finding harness with O(n^(2+ε)) gate cost, QECLean for machine-verified code specification, and QEDist for exact distance certification of stabilizer codes, including fault distance. Architecture-level papers formalize reaction depth, showing constant-depth coherent Boolean arithmetic, and use Block Checks with Pareto tree search for state preparation trade-offs. Formal verification is not common to every item.

ranked.headline: Theory links altermagnetic and noncollinear order to optical, spin-current and magnon probes
ranked.summary: Eight preprints propose measurable signatures of unconventional magnetic order, from magneto-optics and spin photocurrents to magnon thermal Hall and gated magnon devices.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is theoretical identification of responses that expose or exploit unconventional magnetic order. For altermagnets and noncoplanar antiferromagnets, octupolar magneto-optical effects are proposed as field-free probes, and nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent as probes of spin-space symmetry, domains and quantum geometry. Twist engineering of collinear bilayers is proposed to yield quasicrystalline altermagnets with high-order spin polarization. On the magnon side, single magnons and bound magnon pairs in pyrochlore spin-nematics give competing Berry-curvature thermal Hall contributions enabling field-tunable sign reversal; CrI3 nanotubes in an axial field acquire a conical phase and a large pseudo-orbital magnon moment; and gated domain boundaries in BiFeO3 modulate nonreciprocal magnons in a proposed transistor. Cavity photon condensation from scalar spin chirality and defect-enhanced orbital magnetoelectric responses are more peripheral. All items are preprints.

ranked.headline: Compilers target pulse latency, coupling constraints, and native connectivity instead of abstract gate count
ranked.summary: Preprints from Nov 13–19 tie compilation to execution latency, coupling-constrained resynthesis, and non-native graph connectivity, with benchmark gains over Qiskit O3 and EPOC.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is compilation optimized against hardware-level cost rather than abstract gate count. SCOPE guides compilation with an operator Schmidt time surrogate to cut pulse execution latency, and is reported to beat EPOC on 104 benchmarks. The quspect SDK selects routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis, using 0.616x the two-qubit gates of Qiskit O3 on 55 circuits across five targets. For Max-Cut QAOA on non-hardware-native graphs, MinLA surrogates prune interactions to reduce two-qubit depth, and classical configuration recovery restores solution quality. CAVQS adds variational synthesis with QR-based unitary redistribution and dynamic reconstruction using mid-circuit operations. The speed-limit, bounded QSVT inversion, and quantum Hamiltonian descent preprints are algorithmic or theoretical neighbors, not compilation results.

ranked.headline: Forecasts and new statistics test whether upcoming data can separate LCDM from alternatives
ranked.summary: Seven preprints from 12–19 November 2026 forecast how 21-cm, CMB, time-delay and pulsar timing data can discriminate LCDM from alternative models.
ranked.synthesis: Most items quantify how well existing or forthcoming datasets can discriminate LCDM from alternatives, using forecasts and new statistics rather than new measurements. In 21-cm cosmology, persistent homology of Cosmic Dawn brightness maps, the phase gradient spectrum for the squeezed bispectrum, and SKA1-Low forecasts for boosted dark matter each target a distinct observable. Bayesian forecasts for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 ask whether w0waCDM can be separated from LCDM shadow models. The time-delay forecast finds that mass-sheet transformation uncertainties reduce the significance of the decreasing H0 trend to ~1σ. The binaryfog surrogate tests how astrophysical priors affect evidence for new-physics sources in pulsar timing arrays. The Shapley jet-alignment result (4.5σ) is a separate observational large-scale-structure claim.

ranked.headline: Fast emulators and field-level models prepare nonlinear inference for LSST, DESI and FRB data
ranked.summary: Seven preprints from 12–19 November 2026 supply emulators, differentiable codes and new probes for survey-era analyses of structure, dark energy and gravity.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is modeling infrastructure for survey-era inference. A Hi-COLA-trained emulator gives the nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity for LSST Year 1 weak lensing and clustering. bihalofit-JAX provides a differentiable, open-source nonlinear bispectrum and projected statistics, reported to run orders of magnitude faster than existing approaches. A cubic-order EFT forward model of the Lyman-alpha forest, validated on CAMELS and Sherwood, yields BAO shift predictions and simulation-based priors. A second thread uses alternative probes: a physics-informed neural network reconstructs the dark energy equation of state and growth index from DESI DR2 and other data to test GR, while fast radio bursts constrain baryon distribution with IllustrisTNG and Ωm–w from 125 localized bursts. The QCD equation-of-state study of early-universe expansion and stochastic gravitational waves is peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Posterior reuse, GPU samplers and ML components scale inference for upcoming cosmological surveys
ranked.summary: Preprints on dark-siren, LISA, Euclid, LSST and SKA pipelines address efficient sampling, ML components and validation ahead of large datasets.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is building and validating inference infrastructure for forthcoming cosmological datasets, though the items do not all concern sampler efficiency. ASPIRE reuses existing posteriors for joint cosmological and population inference with dark sirens, reporting 6-28x speedups over reanalysis. samsara++ implements trans-dimensional MCMC in C++/CUDA for LISA global fits with overlapping Galactic binaries and noise. The LSST DESC cluster pipeline is validated on cosmoDC2 mocks, constraining Omega_c and sigma_8 from cluster counts. Euclid studies address ML components: strong-lens detection depends strongly on training-set composition, image format and ensembling, while EuclidFM learns 128-dim embeddings from Q1 photometry. SKA SDC3b compares 16 teams' EoR pipelines and finds inter-team variability, underscoring the need for cross-validation.

ranked.headline: Optical and electrical pulses write skyrmions and compensated order in magnets
ranked.summary: Six November 2026 preprints show picosecond optical and electrical writing of compensated or antiferromagnetic order, with NV and pulsed-field MOKE probes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is deterministic writing of magnetic order by ultrafast optical or electrical stimuli. Picosecond circularly polarized pulses write fixed-chirality Néel skyrmions in Co/Pt, with chirality set by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Laser pulses imprint antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer within picoseconds. Atomistic simulations find all-optical helicity-independent switching in GdCo with as little as 1.5 at.% Gd. In triangular artificial spin ice, spin-orbit torque switching and planar Hall readout address a compensated state electrically. Two probe-oriented studies connect more loosely: pulsed-field MOKE up to 60 T on the metamagnetic transition in Fe2Mo3O8, and NV magnetometry of thermally activated switching and zero-field bistability in antiferromagnetic CrPS4 trilayers.

ranked.headline: Scalar-field dark energy models tested against DESI BAO, CMB and supernova data
ranked.summary: New fits of axion and double-power scalar-field dark energy to DESI BAO, CMB and SN data coincide with BAO and low-z supernova probe developments.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is testing dark energy beyond a fixed positive cosmological constant with current distance and growth data. One analysis fits axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant to DES, DESI BAO, CMB and growth data and finds no compelling evidence for a negative value. Another tests a single canonical scalar field with a double-power potential as unified early and late dark energy against CMB, DESI BAO and Pantheon+, reporting a raised H0. Probe-side items are complementary: an all-sky cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey give BAO distance constraints consistent with DESI DR2, and a proposed Rubin twilight program for nearby Type Ia supernovae improves the dark-energy figure of merit in simulations. The decihertz eccentric IMRI paper concerns gravitational-wave template bias and is outside this thread.

ranked.headline: Euclid DR1 calibration chains for NIR imaging, astrometry, spectroscopy and ground-based colours are documented
ranked.summary: Five Euclid DR1 preprints dated 12 November 2026 document the calibration and processing chains that underpin the release.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the instrument-level processing and calibration behind Euclid DR1. The papers describe NISP near-infrared processing and data products, NIR astrometric calibration (distortion modelling, quality control, residuals against Gaia DR3 reaching 30 mas), and SIR spectroscopic calibration, which models the focal plane globally to meet wavelength and flux requirements. Ground-based optical imaging over about 2500 deg2 supplies colours, with photometric stability and depth validated for photo-z and PSF calibration. A calibration strategy paper reviews plan design, implementation and performance against requirements, covering flux, astrometry, PSF, shear and wavelength corrections. What is new is the documented performance of these chains at DR1 scale. The items present pipelines and validation, not cosmological constraints.

ranked.headline: Simulation tests of EFT, halo-model and baryonification predictions for cross-correlated tracers
ranked.summary: Five November 2026 preprints test theoretical models for tracer cross-correlations against simulations, ahead of DESI and SPHEREx analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is checking theoretical models of tracer auto- and cross-correlations against simulations. Two Lyman-alpha papers test effective field theory: a minimal tree-level EFT for 21 cm and Lyα auto- and cross-spectra at z=2.4-4.2 that constrains the HI and Lyα biases, and a full-shape power spectrum and bispectrum analysis validated on AbacusSummit mocks at z=2.5 for DESI. The SPHEREx pair forecasts cross-correlations of extragalactic background light with CMB lensing; the second paper reports halo-model predictions that match lightcone simulations. The baryonification paper offers two methods for producing thermal SZ Compton-y maps from dark-matter-only lightcones. New here is validation spanning line-intensity, forest, lensing and SZ observables, rather than a single probe.

ranked.headline: Resonance engineering in dielectric, perovskite and plasmonic structures sets optical response
ranked.summary: Five preprints from 13–18 November 2026 report quantified resonance control via coupling, material choice and environment in metasurfaces, resonators and nanoantennas.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is control of resonant optical response through coupling, composition or environment. In silicon BIC metasurfaces, strong QBIC-GMR coupling yields intrinsic circular dichroism of 0.995 with Q = 1083 at 1653.9 nm. MAPbBr3 BIC resonances are tuned reversibly and continuously by HCl/HBr vapor anion exchange. Coupled TiO2 and perovskite-coated microresonators show tunable whispering gallery mode hybridization, with non-monotonic behavior reported. In plasmonics, hollow-core fiber-coupled nanoantenna arrays deliver polarization-resilient THz generation and detection (2.1 mW, 145 dB), while a coaxial nanoantenna study maps inverse Faraday magnetization across Au, Ag, Cu, Al and TiN. The new element is the quantified tuning of resonances across platforms, spanning chiral response, chemical reconfiguration and THz instrumentation. Most results are numerical or theoretical, except where experimental metrics are stated.

ranked.headline: Error-aware computation and readout recover optical information from constrained measurements
ranked.summary: Five preprints target specific error sources or resource bottlenecks in turbulence-resilient transmission, single-pixel imaging, ptychography and hyperspectral microscopy.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is recovering optical field information from constrained or imperfect measurements through computation or engineered illumination and readout. Active convolved illumination is reviewed as a way to preserve mode structure through turbulent media using segmented reciprocal-space control. Two single-pixel imaging preprints treat measurement imperfections differently: a Fourier-domain response-matrix correction addresses quantization errors in binary-encoded Fourier acquisition, while a unified calibration and composite-readout framework turns temporal mixing into a measurement resource. A stochastic gradient descent framework for X-ray ptychography reduces peak GPU memory to 65% and time to 22% versus the comparison method. Event-camera Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy with continuous birefringent interferometer scanning reaches real-time widefield spectral acquisition. Modalities differ; the novelty lies in targeted treatment of specific error sources or resource bottlenecks within each.

ranked.headline: Magnetic and ferroelectric order switch valley and exciton states in 2D materials
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show optical, electrical and magnetic switching of valley and exciton states in van der Waals stacks.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is using an ordered degree of freedom as an external handle on excitonic and valley states in van der Waals materials. In rhombohedrally stacked bilayer WSe2, sliding ferroelectricity gives electrically switchable, hysteretic exciton photoluminescence and Raman response, and in few-layer R-stacked WSe2 it switches dipolar exciton transport and drives dipole reconfiguration toward quadrupolar excitons. In WS2/CrSBr heterostructures, type-II band alignment, magnetic-proximity Zeeman valley splitting and spin-selective interlayer charge transfer couple valley and magnetic excitons. In WSe2/CrPS4, a light-controlled Néel vector switches valley polarization optically via spin-polarized charge transfer. The NbOCl2 preprint reports room-temperature antiferroelectricity with reversible switching, probed by SHG, but does not address valley or exciton states directly. What is new is the breadth of switchable order parameters, magnetic, ferroelectric and optical, used to control valley and exciton states.

ranked.headline: Disorder shapes Hall plateaus and orbital Hall currents in topological materials
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show disorder actively shaping transport responses, from Hall plateaus in twisted MoTe2 to orbital Hall currents in amorphous graphene.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that disorder is treated as an active ingredient of transport rather than a perturbation to be neglected, although the multi-Weyl study addresses scattering beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation rather than disorder directly. In twisted bilayer MoTe2 Chern insulators, layer-dependent disorder is reported to shape the widths and transitions of integer and fractional Hall plateaus. A Kubo-Bastin Chebyshev study of a centrosymmetric sp3 tight-binding square lattice examines how the quadrupole-origin orbital Hall effect responds to disorder and how it can be tuned. A generalized semiclassical Boltzmann analysis of multi-Weyl semimetals incorporates orbital moment and intervalley scattering, with monopole charge N as a parameter. The newest item reports that structural and electrostatic disorder, including in amorphous graphene, generates sizable orbital Hall currents absent in pristine systems. What is new is the emphasis on orbital Hall currents arising from disorder itself, rather than only modifying clean-limit responses.

ranked.headline: Josephson junctions engineered beyond the sinusoidal current-phase relation in qubits
ranked.summary: Superconducting qubit platforms now target non-sinusoidal junction transport, from higher harmonics to gate-tunable Andreev spin states.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is treating Josephson junction current-phase transport as a design variable rather than assuming an ideal sinusoidal relation. A proposal for noise-protected superconducting qutrits uses the second harmonic of the current-phase relation in three-junction loops with altermagnetic elements. A study of Al/AlOx/Al tunnel junctions examines non-ergodic area scaling of Andreev transport against the sinusoidal ideal. Gatemon work reports in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire junctions with gate tunability over GHz and coherent control, with T1 of about 0.2-1 us. Planar Ge Josephson junctions show gate-tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits that is independent of junction width, unlike InAs. What is new is the range of materials platforms and deliberate departures from conventional junction behavior. All four items are preprints, and their scope and maturity differ.

ranked.headline: Exact solvability meets non-Hermitian, disordered and hyperbolic lattice spectra
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply exact solvability to non-Hermitian, disordered and hyperbolic lattice models, probing exceptional spectra, fragmentation and localization.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is exact or analytically controlled analysis of lattice models whose spectra or localization depart from Hermitian, translation-invariant behavior. An exactly solvable non-Hermitian Kitaev chain with unequal pairing amplitudes shows an exceptional point where many-body energies collapse, together with Lifshitz criticality. Non-Hermitian fermionic chains with random imaginary gauge fields display erratic skin localization and density fragmentation into Fermi domains. A disordered spin-1 chain with an exact binary-tree Fock-space structure rigorously bounds spreading at strong disorder. The three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic periodic-boundary clusters is analyzed through ground-state flux sectors and two-vison gaps. The new element is the combination of exact solvability with diagnostics of exceptional spectra, fragmentation and localization across non-Hermitian, disordered and hyperbolic-geometry settings.

ranked.headline: Engineered photonic lattices control flat bands, BICs, mobility edges and edge states
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair non-Hermitian coupling and quasicrystal experiments to tune flatband, BIC and mobility-edge physics in photonic systems.
ranked.synthesis: Four preprints use engineered photonic structures to control how optical modes are localized or confined. Two are model-based: a four-mode non-Hermitian description of C2-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs, where coupling sign governs BIC merging and flatband formation with reported Q scaling as k^-6, and a one-dimensional non-Hermitian pseudospin lattice in which non-Hermiticity embeds compact localized states in a continuum. An experimental preprint reports exact mobility edges and flat-band states in a two-dimensional photonic quasicrystal realized with auxiliary subsystems and photonic waveguides. A fourth proposal targets antihelical gapless edge states in a photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy, which concerns edge states rather than flat bands. The new element is explicit tuning of flatband and BIC physics through coupling sign and non-Hermiticity, alongside experimental verification of exact mobility edges.

ranked.headline: Spectral control of thermal emission via multilayers, gap modes and material data
ranked.summary: Numerical emitter and absorber studies and a new AM0 property database target wavelength-selective thermal radiation for energy conversion.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is wavelength-resolved control of thermal radiation, where absorption, emission and reflection set energy conversion performance. A 16-layer MgO/Si multilayer on tungsten is inverse-designed as a selective emitter for GaSb thermophotovoltaic cells, with a modeled conversion efficiency of 47.0%. A gold-carbon metasurface uses a dielectric spacer to tune gap-mode overlap with carbon, sharpening the infrared roll-off in solar-thermal absorbers. The SpaderOptics database provides reflectivity, absorptivity and emissivity for 21 materials under the AM0 solar spectrum, relevant to absorber and emitter design. The photonic Maxwell's demon proposal, which uses one-way dielectric mirrors and wavelength-converting materials in a 3D box to accumulate blackbody radiation, is less directly tied to this design thread. The new elements are inverse design of a multilayer emitter, spacer-based gap-mode tuning, and a property database under AM0 illumination. All four items are numerical or proposal-stage.

ranked.headline: Accidental BICs in photonic systems tied to parity and nonlocal scattering zeros
ranked.summary: Recent preprints refine how accidental BICs arise, linking them to radiation-source parity and spatial nonlocality in photonic structures.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the characterization of bound states in the continuum (BICs), localized modes that remain confined within the radiation continuum of open photonic systems. Two preprints address accidental BICs directly. One reports that in vertically asymmetric photonic lattices they are governed by radiation-source parity and can be recovered through parity restoration. The other models metasurface BICs as converging reflection and transmission zeros and concludes that accidental BICs require spatially nonlocal response. A third preprint examines Berry phase and topological quasi-bound states in Möbius resonators, reporting a mode-dependent phase. The fourth item, on hybrid graphene plasmon-silica phonon eigenmodes in a graphene ring, is a plasmonic system forming quadrupolar eigenmodes and multiband vortex states, and it is less directly tied to the BIC framing. The new element is the framing of accidental BIC existence in terms of parity and nonlocality.

ranked.headline: Wavefunction zeros and overlap determinants diagnose Chern and Z2 topology in lattice models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints move topological diagnostics from bulk spectra toward wavefunction zeros, overlap determinants and localizer operators.
ranked.synthesis: Three of the four preprints diagnose topological invariants through objects other than the bulk Hamiltonian spectrum: zeros of the occupied-subspace overlap determinant for relative Chern and Z2 invariants (arXiv:2611.25037), wavefunction zeros and vorticities enforced by crystalline symmetry and readable from band-dispersion shifts (arXiv:2611.25028), and spectral localizer operators unifying Z and Z2 invariants for hinge modes, Dirac nodes and valley boundary modes (arXiv:2611.26160). The shared novelty is the shift of the diagnostic object toward overlaps, zeros and localizers. arXiv:2611.19328 applies a related logic to dynamical quantum phase transitions, attributing boundary effects to edge modes of the non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrix rather than Hamiltonian topology. It concerns dynamics rather than ground-state band topology and is the least direct fit to the dominant thread.

ranked.headline: Compact platforms achieve nonreciprocal, tunable and confined optical responses
ranked.summary: Recent work extends optical response control beyond static, reciprocal, linear behavior in compact geometries.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the control of optical response beyond static, reciprocal, linear behavior in compact geometries. Two items address nonreciprocity directly: a computational study of integrated isolators built from nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors using spin-momentum locking, including an all-optical isolator proposal, and a temporally modulated Floquet metasurface of three closely spaced conducting sheets that shows asymmetric frequency conversion, reported as violating Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation. A tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonic device with CrCl3 provides tunable coupling via hierarchical anti-crossing and reduced magnon loss in experiment. An inverse-designed transparent conducting oxide cavity at the epsilon-near-zero point reports stronger confinement and faster dynamics. The novelty lies in joint control of nonreciprocity, modulation, and coupling within compact platforms. The items differ in method and maturity and do not share a single mechanism.

ranked.headline: Interfaces tune spin transport, terahertz emission and molecule-TMD interlayer coupling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that interfacial layers, from thermal annealing to monolayer MoSe2, measurably alter spin and terahertz response.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the role of an interface between a functional spin or optical layer and an adjacent organic, molecular, or two-dimensional layer in governing transport and optical response. In NDI-based organic spin valves with Co/Au or graphene/Co/Au electrodes, in situ thermal annealing degrades magnetoresistance, pointing to thermally driven reorganization at the interface as a controlling factor for charge and spin transport. Monolayer MoSe2 covering Py/Au or Py/Pt spintronic terahertz emitters attenuates the emitted amplitude about fourfold, attributed to absorption by free carriers. Optical spectroscopy of non-planar spin-crossover molecules on monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides shows efficient interlayer coupling via Förster energy transfer. The new element is the use of a monolayer TMD as an active overlayer that modulates spintronic terahertz emission, alongside evidence of efficient molecule-TMD interlayer coupling. The organic spin valve study does not share the same spectroscopic or terahertz setting, so the link is interfacial rather than mechanistic.

ranked.headline: Surrogate and differentiable models accelerate integrated photonic design loops
ranked.summary: Costly full-physics simulation motivates open-source workflows and differentiable surrogates that speed up photonic device design.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of computational workflows and learned or differentiable surrogate models to shorten integrated photonic design loops. TARANG, an open-source Python workflow, carries refractive indices through to GDSII masks for silicon nitride microcomb chips and reports validated dispersion. A neural network surrogate, trained on double-pulse femtosecond laser simulations, predicts optothermal observables for thin silicon films on fused silica, enabling rapid design exploration. A differentiable coupled-mode-theory surrogate supports gradient-based inverse design of multimode waveguides, reducing transmission error by 17-37% relative to forward EME on TFLN. What is new across these works is the reliance on surrogate or end-to-end differentiable formulations, although the three address distinct material platforms and physical regimes.

ranked.headline: Full characterization of optical skyrmions and entangled biphoton spectra
ranked.summary: Analytical and optimization methods now target complete, rather than partial, characterization of structured optical states.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the complete characterization of structured optical degrees of freedom. One preprint defines full-skyrmionic polarimetry and a multi-stage optimization framework that uses topological evaluating functions to measure optical skyrmions accurately. A second preprint analytically computes the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of SPDC biphotons with a generating-function method, enabling efficient evaluation of high-dimensional entangled states. A third preprint, on backward-scattering photoelectron holography in polar CO driven by sub-cycle laser pulses, addresses molecular strong-field dynamics rather than light-state metrology. It is included because it separates forward and backward scattering fringes, but it does not share the light-state focus of the other two. What is new is the emphasis on exhaustive rather than partial characterization, signaled by the word full in two titles.
